program.name: Iliad
program.organization: Iliad (fiscally sponsored by Principles of Intelligence)
program.cohort: November 2026 Iliad Intensive / December 2026 Iliad Fellowship
program.roundStatusEvidence: Calendar: "November 2026 Iliad Intensive | Nov 2–27, 2026 | London | Applications close Sep 28, 2026" and "December 2026 Iliad Fellowship | Dec 1–Mar 5, 2027 | Bay Area | Applications close Oct 19, 2026"
program.nextRoundNote: The Intensive runs monthly, alternating between London and the Bay Area.
program.locationNotes: November 2026 Intensive at LISA, London. December 2026 Fellowship: the form labels it "[London or SF]" but the calendar lists "Bay Area" (feed venue: Lighthaven). No visa-sponsorship policy stated; the form asks for immigration status in the US and/or UK.
program.compensation: Intensive: no tuition, $5,000 USD travel-and-housing allowance, office space, lunch and dinner five days a week. Fellowship: $6,000 USD travel-and-housing allowance per month.
program.commitment: Intensive: full-time, four weeks, five days a week 10am–6pm. Fellowship: full-time, three months (calendar feed describes the December 2026 Fellowship as 14 weeks).
eligibilityNotes: Applicants must confirm they will be at least 18 by the start date of every program they apply to.

Intensive: strong mathematical background, typically pursuing or having completed a graduate degree in mathematics, physics, or theoretical computer science; "The requirement is mathematical maturity, not a specific credential."
Fellowship: aimed at PhD students, postdocs, or researchers with equivalent experience; the degree is not a hard requirement. Completing the Intensive first is not required.
Immigration status in the US and/or UK is asked; no sponsorship or work-authorization rule is published.

aiPolicy.summary: No policy on AI use in applications appears on the apply form or on the program, FAQ, or calendar pages.

stages.name: Application form
stages.description: Single on-page form on iliad.ac/apply covering upcoming Intensive and Fellowship iterations: CV, program choice, three written answers (why applying, career aspirations, two difficult mathematical concepts), immigration status, how you heard, and age/privacy confirmations. Confirmation email comes from admissions@iliad.ac.

stages.name: Later selection stages
stages.description: Not described on any Iliad page.

sources.label: Apply page (native form)
sources.note: Form is native HTML on the page (no embedded third-party form); submissions POST to an Iliad Cloudflare worker. Validation rules read from the page script. The calendar's link https://www.iliad.ac/apply?direct loads the same form ("direct" is stored as a referral slug).

sources.label: Calendar / Upcoming Events
sources.note: Rendered status per event: Nov 2026 Intensive "Applications close Sep 28, 2026"; Dec 2026 Fellowship "Applications close Oct 19, 2026"; Oct 2026 Intensive, Oct 2026 Fellowship, Nov 2026 Fellowship "Applications closed".

sources.note: Duration, schedule, locations, allowance, who should apply.

sources.label: FAQ
sources.note: "A single Iliad application form covers upcoming Intensive and Fellowship iterations." PhD not required.

program.notes: One form covers both the November 2026 Intensive (deadline Sep 28, 2026) and the December 2026 Fellowship (deadline Oct 19, 2026); the round stays open until the later one. Neither deadline states a timezone; each is recorded as end of day where that cohort runs (London, then the Bay Area). The November 2026 Fellowship appears in the calendar but is not offered on the form and shows “Applications closed”. No per-question length limits are shown to applicants.

questions.notes: PDF only (Word documents rejected by the form script); max 4.5 MB.

questions.prompt: I would like to be considered for the:
questions.notes: Checkboxes; at least one must be selected ("Please select at least one program."). Location tags on the form ("[London or SF]" for the December Fellowship) differ from the calendar, which lists the December 2026 Fellowship in the Bay Area (venue Lighthaven).

questions.prompt: Why are you applying to this program?

questions.notes: Hidden HTML maxlength=50000 characters (not shown to applicants).

questions.notes: Asks for exactly two concepts plus what made them difficult; no length limit shown. Hidden HTML maxlength=50000 characters (not shown to applicants).
